report.summary: Chunk 3 of 14: defines _jsonable, _existing_ancestor, _as_predicate, _read_gitdir_pointer, constants; contains comments about moved symbols and git config.
risks: _jsonable | low | Unserialisable values are degraded to repr; may mask errors but prevents abort. | Verify that repr output is acceptable for ledger writes.
_as_predicate | low | A token that raises is treated as 'not cancelled'; may mask cancellation failures. | Confirm that this behaviour is intended.
_read_gitdir_pointer | medium | Returns None for unusual shapes; caller may misidentify a linked worktree. | Ensure callers handle None correctly and don't assume safety.

handoff.purpose: Define utility functions and constants for serialisation, cancellation, and git worktree detection.

symbols.name: _jsonable
symbols.note: Coerce value to JSON-acceptable types; degrades unserialisable values to repr.

symbols.name: _existing_ancestor
symbols.note: Alias for nearest_existing; finds nearest existing ancestor directory.

symbols.name: _as_predicate
symbols.note: Normalise cancel token to zero-arg predicate; treats raising tokens as not cancelled.

symbols.name: _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG
symbols.note: Tuple of git config keys that name programs to execute; pinned empty.

symbols.name: _read_gitdir_pointer
symbols.note: Reads .git file in linked worktree to find admin directory; returns None on failure.

claims.text: A caller's metadata must never be able to abort an attempt: an unserialisable value is degraded to its repr rather than raising out of the ledger write, which would strand the attempt between intent and effect.
claims.why: The function returns repr(value) for unsupported types, never raises.

claims.text: Walking up asks the question that was actually meant: does the VOLUME have room -- and it asks it without creating anything, so the storage check stays side-effect free.
claims.why: The docstring describes behaviour of nearest_existing, which is defined outside this chunk; the alias does not implement the walk.

claims.text: This was a third private copy of the same walk (the fence needs it to find the GROUND a not-yet-created file will land on). Same function, same semantics, so it is an alias rather than a reimplementation.
claims.why: Refers to external code (nearest_existing, fence) not present in chunk.

claims.text: A token that raises is treated as 'not cancelled': a broken token must not be able to abort work it was only supposed to observe.
claims.why: Both _call and _event catch Exception and return False.

claims.text: Every one of them is pinned empty on the command line, where no config file can override it. See :func:`_git` for the measurement that made this necessary.
claims.why: Refers to _git function not in this chunk; claim about pinning is not verifiable here.

claims.text: A linked worktree's .git is a FILE containing 'gitdir: <abs path>'. Read once, before any candidate code exists, so later git invocations can name the directory explicitly instead of re-resolving a pointer the candidate may since have rewritten.
claims.why: The function reads the file and extracts the path after 'gitdir:'.

claims.text: Returns None when the shape is not the expected one -- a plain directory (an ordinary clone rather than a linked worktree), a missing file, or an unreadable one. None means 'do not pin', which leaves git's normal discovery in place; it is the pre-existing behaviour, so a caller is never worse off than before this existed. It is emphatically NOT a claim that the worktree is safe.
claims.why: Function returns None if directory, OSError, or not starting with 'gitdir:'.

claims.text: They must be carried over, and that was measured rather than foreseen. Emptying GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL removes core.autocrlf along with everything else, and on Windows that setting is what makes a CRLF working tree compare equal to an LF index.
claims.why: Refers to external behaviour (Windows CRLF) and measurements not in chunk.

observations.what: _jsonable handles Mapping, list, tuple, set, frozenset; note that set and frozenset are converted to list, losing order determinism.
_as_predicate uses try-except to swallow exceptions; the docstring claims this is intentional.
_read_gitdir_pointer returns Path for directory .git, not None; docstring says returns None for plain directory, but code returns Path if is_dir(). Possible inconsistency.
Comment states _identity and _overlap_reason used to be defined here; now imported from daedalus.primary_tree. No import statement visible in chunk.
